title: Complete public, generic, persisted, corpus, and consumer inventory for typed formats

authority.inventory_role: This artifact records the live evidence baseline under the accepted ADR. It is not a new design authority and cannot authorize dependency removal, format removal, migration, or cutover.

policy.coverage_rule: Every direct serde_json, rmp-serde, and bincode-next token in a scanned Rust root is covered by a pinned lexical count and a root classification. Production persisted or public/generic uses are additionally covered by an explicit surface, format profile, consumer, and corpus row.
policy.arbitrary_serde_rule: T: Serialize and T: DeserializeOwned remain first-class downstream inputs. A finite fixture roster cannot narrow the Serde data model or imply a whitelist.
policy.exact_bytes_rule: EXACT_BYTES means existing accepted bytes must remain readable and byte-producing behavior may be compatibility-sensitive. SEMANTIC means equivalent values are required but map order, whitespace, or backend byte choices are not claimed stable.
policy.unknown_rule: Any missing reader, historical corpus, compatibility classification, resource bound, canonical-order rule, version rule, migration reader, or downstream owner is UNKNOWN_BLOCKING. Unknown evidence cannot be silently converted into a design assumption.
policy.custom_rule: SerializationFormat::Custom byte 255 and downstream Serializer and Deserializer injection stay public. The current standalone non-Serde codec fixture proves that injection path, while SerdeCodec rejecting Custom remains intentional and no finite fixture proves arbitrary downstream replacement parity.
policy.no_cutover_rule: This A1 inventory changes no encoder, decoder, schema, dependency, public symbol, discriminant, persisted byte, or error behavior.

format_profiles.canonical_ordering: Struct field order follows Serde; unordered map iteration is not canonicalized by SerdeCodec. Persisted trace shapes must not infer general map canonicality.
format_profiles.resource_bounds: SerdeCodec itself has no input-length cap. TypedSymbol applies its envelope cap. Trace readers apply per-metadata, per-event, compressed-chunk, and preallocation caps.
format_profiles.error_contract: Public SerdeCodec owns stringified SerializationError and DeserializationError. ReplayTrace::to_bytes exposes rmp_serde::encode::Error; ReplayTrace::from_bytes owns ReplayDecodeError containing rmp decode failures.
format_profiles.version_policy: No generic payload version byte. TypedSymbol, trace-file, replay-metadata, and streaming containers own their versions.
format_profiles.migration_policy: The standalone downstream fixture pins one current rmp-serde 1.3.1 payload golden. Existing trace MessagePack remains readable, but no prior-release committed byte corpus or proven historical migration reader exists.

format_profiles.canonical_ordering: Every production call uses bincode::config::legacy(); collection order is inherited from the serialized type and is not globally canonicalized.
format_profiles.resource_bounds: SerdeCodec itself has no decode byte limit and ignores trailing decoded bytes. TypedSymbol bounds its payload; distributed snapshot bounds its owned framing before vector-clock decode.
format_profiles.error_contract: Public SerdeCodec stringifies bincode EncodeError and DecodeError into owned errors. Distributed snapshot maps codec failures into SnapshotError.
format_profiles.version_policy: No generic payload version byte. TypedSymbol owns its header version; distributed snapshot v2 owns the Bincode vector-clock field.
format_profiles.migration_policy: The legacy configuration is part of the accepted baseline, and the standalone downstream fixture pins one current bincode-next 3.1.1 legacy-config payload golden. There is no prior-release committed Bincode corpus or cross-version migration reader.

format_profiles.canonical_ordering: Serde struct field order is stable for a fixed type; map order, pretty whitespace, and ad hoc Value construction are not globally canonical. Exact bytes are claimed only where bytes feed a stored hash or a specifically versioned artifact contract.
format_profiles.resource_bounds: SerdeCodec has no byte cap. Individual persisted readers own validation and resource policy; the inventory does not infer one global JSON limit.
format_profiles.error_contract: SerdeCodec owns stringified errors. Other public JSON helpers may expose serde_json::Error or their module-owned validation errors as recorded per surface.
format_profiles.version_policy: No generic JSON envelope. Each persisted JSON family owns its schema field or constant.
format_profiles.migration_policy: Semantic additive evolution is the default. Existing versioned artifact readers remain required; no global JSON migration exists.

format_profiles.backend: downstream Serializer<T> and Deserializer<T> implementations injected into TypedEncoder and TypedDecoder
format_profiles.resource_bounds: Downstream codec plus TypedSymbol envelope; SerdeCodec intentionally rejects Custom.
format_profiles.error_contract: Downstream codec returns Asupersync-owned SerializationError or DeserializationError.
format_profiles.version_policy: TypedSymbol header carries version, type id, format byte, schema hash, and payload length; payload versioning remains downstream-defined.
format_profiles.migration_policy: The standalone baseline consumer implements a non-Serde codec, exercises Custom byte 255 through the single-symbol path, and fences explicit typed-symbol versions. Its finite current fixture does not prove arbitrary downstream payload migration, ordering, or resource parity.

generic_dependency_decisions.rationale: Owning a general-purpose Serde MessagePack implementation would require preserving the complete downstream data model, diagnostics, resource behavior, and ergonomics represented by 3,207 incumbent Rust source lines. No in-repository finite codec can establish that parity, while the pure-Rust incumbent already satisfies the public capability.

generic_dependency_decisions.no_claim_boundary: KEEP changes no production source, dependency, public variant, discriminant, persisted format, or migration policy and does not prove historical artifact readability or unordered-map byte canonicality.

public_generic_surfaces.generic_contract: Arbitrary downstream T: Serialize and T: DeserializeOwned; no seal, registry allow-list, derive requirement, or finite schema roster.
TypeRegistry derives a deterministic u64 schema hash from Rust type_name<T> and u32 version. TypedEncoder defaults to version 1 and permits downstream codec injection.

persisted_surfaces.backend: Selected SerializationFormat backend or downstream Custom codec
persisted_surfaces.exactness_detail: 27-byte TSYM header: magic[4], u16 LE version, u64 LE type id, u8 format, u64 LE schema hash, u32 LE payload length. Discriminants are 1, 2, 3, and 255. Payload compatibility then follows the selected backend.
persisted_surfaces.canonical_ordering: Header canonical; payload not globally canonical for arbitrary Serde maps.
persisted_surfaces.resource_bounds: Payload <= DEFAULT_SYMBOL_SIZE - 27 and representable as u32.
persisted_surfaces.version_policy: Header version defaults to 1; type id and schema hash are derived from type_name<T> and version.
persisted_surfaces.migration_policy: Published v0.3.9 typed symbols used build-sensitive Rust TypeId hashing. Current readers admit those exact headers only through a trusted version-provenanced LegacyTypedSymbolIdentity tuple, decode the generic payload with its recorded backend, and rewrite a distinct current stable-header artifact while retaining the source rollback bytes. This is not a general type-rename or schema-alias registry.
persisted_surfaces.no_claim_boundary: The pinned v0.3.9 MessagePack and Bincode records prove only the exact published-writer type and provenance tuple; they do not prove arbitrary third-party type identity portability across old Rust toolchains.

persisted_surfaces.backend: Owned ASUPERTRACE v3 container with MessagePack metadata/events, optional LZ4 chunks, and SHA-256 metadata/event-stream integrity
persisted_surfaces.exactness_detail: Magic ASUPERTRACE, u16 LE file version 3, flags/compression framing, SHA-256 metadata digest, event count, SHA-256 canonical uncompressed event-frame digest, and length-delimited MessagePack records.
persisted_surfaces.canonical_ordering: Container order is append order; event/metadata struct field encoding follows rmp-serde. General map canonicality is not claimed.
persisted_surfaces.resource_bounds: metadata <= 1 MiB; event <= 16 MiB; compressed or uncompressed chunk <= 64 MiB; event preallocation <= 10,000,000.
persisted_surfaces.version_policy: Writers emit v3; ordinary, streaming, and integrity readers reject versions outside 1..=3 and admit supported v1/v2 containers; the raw-record compatibility inspector admits only uncompressed v1/v2/v3 framing; embedded replay metadata must equal schema version 1.
persisted_surfaces.error_contract: TraceFileError owns I/O, magic, version, flags, length, compression, MessagePack, schema, checksum, and non-overwriting migration failures; ordinary compatibility reads reject unknown records without skipping.
persisted_surfaces.migration_policy: migrate_trace_file and trace migrate stream a legacy v1/v2 source into a sibling staging file, sync it, atomically publish a distinct non-existing v3 destination, preserve event order/count and the untouched source rollback anchor, and clean staging without exposing partial output on malformed input or write failure. recover_trace_prefix returns only a caller-bounded contiguous prefix with Complete, Partial, or LimitReached status.
persisted_surfaces.no_claim_boundary: The published v0.3.9 v2 boundary and large trace fixtures prove current ordinary/streaming readers, migration, replay, and CLI paths for those exact artifacts only; they do not prove arbitrary earlier releases or performance.

persisted_surfaces.exactness_detail: Raw MessagePack blob whose TraceMetadata.version must exactly equal REPLAY_SCHEMA_VERSION 1.
persisted_surfaces.canonical_ordering: Replay event vector order is significant; general map canonicality is not claimed.
persisted_surfaces.resource_bounds: Raw ReplayTrace::from_bytes has no module-level byte cap; file/streaming envelopes own their bounds.
persisted_surfaces.error_contract: Public encode returns rmp_serde::encode::Error; decode returns owned ReplayDecodeError with MessagePack and version cases.
persisted_surfaces.migration_policy: Replay schema 1 remains current. The committed published-v0.3.9 schema-1 blob is decoded directly by the current reader; malformed bytes and any other schema version fail closed.
persisted_surfaces.no_claim_boundary: The published v0.3.9 blob proves compatibility only for replay schema 1 and its recorded semantics, not an unimplemented lower-version migration.

persisted_surfaces.exactness_detail: StreamingReplayer consumes the ordered ASUPERTRACE event frames through TraceReader, including v3 event-stream checksum admission; checkpoint data remains independently length-delimited MessagePack.
persisted_surfaces.canonical_ordering: Record order and sequence numbers are significant.
persisted_surfaces.resource_bounds: Trace-file metadata/event/chunk bounds apply to StreamingReplayer; standalone evidence chunks have an explicit max_chunk_bytes bound and checkpoint allocation remains separately bounded by its decoder.
persisted_surfaces.version_policy: StreamingReplayer inherits v1/v2 read and strict v3 checksum/version policy from TraceReader; replay schema metadata remains the semantic version owner.
persisted_surfaces.error_contract: StreamingReplayError wraps strict TraceFileError, I/O, checkpoint, divergence, MessagePack, record-size, and backpressure failures.
persisted_surfaces.migration_policy: The A7 E2E streams the committed published-v0.3.9 v2 trace before and after atomic non-overwriting v3 migration; the large published-writer recipe separately exercises 4,096 events.
persisted_surfaces.no_claim_boundary: The pinned v0.3.9 v2 fixtures prove bounded streaming compatibility for those exact event sets, not every historical release or throughput.
